description: Verify debounced button-to-LED toggle on D2/D13 with ON/OFF reporting on Serial1, including fast reaction and single-toggle-per-bouncy-press behavior.

steps.requirement: The LED is off immediately after reset.
A clean button press turns the LED on (exactly one toggle edge).
The LED reacts quickly to a button press (within 50 ms, no noticeable delay).
On turning the LED on, the board prints 'ON' on its own line on Serial1.
A second, bouncy button press turns the LED off with exactly one toggle edge, proving debouncing works.
On turning the LED off, the board prints 'OFF' on its own line on Serial1.

assumptions: "Reacts quickly / no noticeable delay" is graded as an LED response within 50 ms of the button edge, since the handout gives no numeric bound.
A real bouncy press is simulated with 10 contact bounces at 2 ms intervals before settling low; this is treated as a representative bounce pattern since the handout gives no bounce profile.
UART text requirements are checked with a 'contains' match on "ON"/"OFF" rather than an exact full-line regex, to tolerate surrounding whitespace/newline formatting.
The button idle (unpressed) state is simulated by releasing the drive line, relying on the student's INPUT_PULLUP to read it high, matching the handout's wiring (no external resistor).
logic_trace's final_level field is numeric (0 = low, 1 = high).

not_graded.requirement: Debouncing must be implemented in software without blocking delay() calls.
not_graded.reason: Implementation technique (blocking vs non-blocking code, use of millis() timers) cannot be determined from electrical behavior alone.
Source-code style/comments are not observable through electrical measurement.
